pages.text: Mom filled the paddy that evening. Water brimmed.
Dingding watched one rippling spot. Straw drifted toward it. "I hope water stays until morning."
Mom laid a soil lump on the bank and pressed with a foot. "Done. Dinner."
Dingding pointed. "The ripple is still there." "Too dark to see. Tomorrow."
Dingding lay wide awake. Water trickled outside. Stars sparkled.
Morning! Only half the paddy's water remained.
Below was a watery sea. Mr. Ming looked up. "All the water came from above!"
Dingding found the ripple again and scattered a handful of straw.
It gathered in one spot. "Here!" Mom packed soil tightly there.
No more ripple. Straw floated still. Ducks below quacked, perhaps disappointed.
